name: Connection Timestamps
os_min: First Install/Last Connected/Last Removal properties require Windows 7+ (0064) / Windows 8+ (0066, 0067)
location: Plug and Play log — XP: C:\Windows\setupapi.log ; Win7+: C:\Windows\inf\setupapi.dev.log. Registry — Win7+: SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Enum\USBSTOR\Disk&Ven_&Prod_\<USBSerial#>\Properties\{83da6326-97a6-4088-9453-a19231573b29}\####(0064=First Install, 0066=Last Connected, 0067=Last Removal); mirrored under \Enum\SCSI\... . Also Win10+: Microsoft-Windows-Partition/Diagnostic.evtx Event ID 1006 per device connect/disconnect.
purpose: Determines the temporal usage of specific USB devices connected to a Windows machine by combining the plug-and-play log file (first-ever install) with the registry's Properties GUID subkeys (first install, last connected, last removed) and the Partition/Diagnostic event log (every connect/disconnect).
key_fields: setupapi.dev.log entries — search for the device's serial number; log timestamps are in local time zone
Timestamps stored in Windows 64-bit FILETIME format
Partition/Diagnostic Event ID 1006 — recorded for each device connect/disconnect (log cleared during major OS updates)
normal_baseline: Connection timestamps for known, approved removable media align with expected work usage windows and match the device inventory the user is authorized to use.
anomalies: A First Install timestamp for a USB device with no corresponding approval/inventory record, especially shortly before a data-loss incident
A Last Connected/Last Removal pair spanning a very short window immediately followed by evidence of large file transfers, consistent with rapid exfiltration to removable media
setupapi.dev.log entries for a device that has no matching USBSTOR registry key, or vice versa, suggesting partial artifact cleanup
anti_forensic_notes: The Partition/Diagnostic event log is cleared during major Windows OS updates, so its coverage window can be shorter than the registry Properties subkeys, which persist across updates unless the device is fully removed from the registry.
interpretation: This is the correlation layer across three separate data sources: the plug-and-play log gives the very first time a device's driver was ever installed, the Properties GUID subkeys refine that into first/last-connected/last-removed, and Partition/Diagnostic gives a per-event connect/disconnect timeline (when not yet rolled off by an OS update). Use all three together rather than relying on one, since each has a different retention/coverage limitation. See `usb-device-identification` for the broader device-identity fields and `setupapi-devlog` for the log file format itself.
